messages.subject: constrained refined Delaunay triangulation.
parts:
Dear Prof, I am working on spatiotemporal hierarchical Bayesian modeling using RINLA through SPDE approach. We are using constrained refined Delaunay triangulation. I am wondering what happens if we use unconstrained Delaunay triangulation? Would the results vary? If you use a vanilla type of triangle how the results would vary?

 

Best regards;

Anteneh

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] constrained refined Delaunay triangulation.
parts:
Hi,
The “constrained” part is the least relevant; it just means that one can specify that certain polygons/line must be part of the triangulation edges. The only constrained edges are usually the boundary edges. The quality of the spde approximation depends mostly on the “refined” aspect. Meshes with small and well-formed triangles (short edges, and no small acute angles) provide closer approximations. Meshes with large and/or sharp angled triangles exhibit approximation artifacts; the fields are always conditionally deterministic, given the values at the mesh vertices. This, for example, shows up as a non-constant variance. See meshbuilder() in the INLA package for a tool to analyze this effect. (Turn on the mesh assessment checkbox)

Finn
